bank.retain_mission: Extract what a judged Belief says and what it rests on. A Belief is one falsifiable proposition about a supply-chain bottleneck or a company's exposure to one, with an author's judgement (proven, disproven, undecidable), a confidence, an as-of date, and the Facts it cites with their quotes. Keep the proposition as one statement, with its judgement and confidence, who judged it and as of when; keep which cited Facts are for it and which against, with each Fact's company, document and date; keep figures, units, currencies and reporting periods exactly as the quotes give them. A hedged or forward-looking quote stays hedged: a plan, an expectation or a risk is not an outcome. A Belief that was superseded keeps the proposition that replaced it. Do not turn a cited quote into a Belief of its own, and do not infer a judgement the document does not state.

entity_labels.description: The optical supply-chain layer or layers the fact concerns. Give every layer the fact is about, and none when it concerns none of them; a material named alone (indium phosphide, gallium arsenide, silicon photonics) is no layer, and neither is a raw material, metal or mineral (indium, gallium, germanium, rare earths) or its supply, prices or export controls: a layer is a product or a manufacturing step.
